newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs weak in lackluster activity.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs weak in lackluster activity.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices were weaker in dull trade on Tuesday and perceptions of abundant supply of propane, a key LPG, players said.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, spot propane dipped a quarter cent to between 35.00 cents and 35.25 cents a gallon amid no news.
"There is just a lack of interest in the market and not much demand," said a Conway trader.
The summer doldrums also put a lid on propane in Mont Belvieu, Texas, where the product stayed steady at 34.75/35.00 cents, with 34.75 cents trading hands.
A major petrochemical firm was talked pushing down Belvieu isobutane, which shaved a quarter cent off from Monday.
Players said they expected propane stocks to show a large build for the month of June in the Energy Information Administration's late Wednesday report.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
